title: JPMorgan Engages Over 100 Multinationals as GIFT City Emerges as Global Treasury Hub
excerpt: More than 100 companies have approached JPMorgan to set up corporate treasury operations at India's GIFT City, as the financial hub's banking assets cross $100 billion.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Over 100 multinationals are exploring treasury operations at GIFT City with JPMorgan.
  • Banking assets at GIFT City have doubled to over $100 billion in two years.
  • Ten corporate treasury centres are operational at GIFT City, with more expected.
  • JPMorgan offers services to optimize cash management for multinational companies.
  • GIFT City aims to rival global financial hubs like Dubai and Singapore.

  • Over 100 multinational companies have approached JPMorgan Chase to explore banking and payment solutions for treasury operations at GIFT City over the next 12 to 18 months.
  • Banking assets at the Gujarat-based financial hub have more than doubled to over $100 billion in two years, driven by a 20-year tax holiday that took effect in April.
  • Ten corporate treasury centres are already operational at GIFT City, with the next wave expected to be led by multinational firms centralising cash and funding operations.
  • JPMorgan offers physical pooling, cash concentration, and notional pooling services to help companies optimise borrowing costs and deploy surplus cash efficiently.

A Surge of Corporate Interest

More than 100 companies — spanning multinationals, insurance firms, and fintech businesses — have approached JPMorgan Chase & Co. to explore banking and payment solutions for corporate treasury operations at India's GIFT City, the bank disclosed this week.

The inquiries, expected to translate into operational setups over the next 12 to 18 months, represent what JPMorgan's India payments chief called an unprecedented level of interest in the Gujarat International Finance Tec-City.

"We haven't seen anything like this before. Treasury centres are a major theme for GIFT City, and the ability to offer foreign-currency accounts alongside rupee capabilities provides an additional tailwind."

- Guhaprasath Rajagopal, Managing Director and Head of Payments, JPMorgan India

The wave of interest comes as multinational companies look to cut borrowing costs and deploy surplus cash more efficiently, particularly amid volatile commodity prices. Rajagopal told Bloomberg that significant internal evaluation is underway at corporates as they weigh the hub's advantages.

GIFT City's Rapid Growth

Established in Gujarat — Prime Minister Narendra Modi's home state — GIFT City was designed to rival global financial centres such as Dubai, Singapore, and Hong Kong. Its International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) allows companies to transact in foreign currencies, manage global treasury functions, and access international markets under a single regulator, the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA).

The numbers tell the story of its ascent. Banking assets at the hub surpassed $100 billion as of September, more than doubling from two years earlier. A 20-year tax holiday that came into effect in April has further accelerated the inflow of global capital.

Ten corporate treasury centres are already operational at GIFT City, including AMNS Global Treasury Centre IFSC and Amefird Treasury, according to IFSCA data. The regulator and banking executives expect the next wave of growth to come predominantly from multinational companies establishing treasury operations at the hub.

What JPMorgan Is Offering

The expansion is creating fresh business opportunities for banks, particularly in liquidity management — an increasingly critical function as global companies seek to centralise cash and funding operations in a single location.

JPMorgan is offering a suite of treasury services at GIFT City, including physical pooling (consolidating cash balances from subsidiaries into a central account), cash concentration, and notional pooling (offsetting balances across multiple accounts without physically moving funds). These services help companies optimise working capital across their global operations.

JPMorgan's Treasury Services
›Physical Pooling: Consolidates cash balances.
›Cash Concentration: Centralizes cash management.
›Notional Pooling: Offsets balances across accounts.
›Optimizes working capital for global operations.

The Wall Street bank inaugurated its international banking unit at GIFT City in 2022. It has since expanded its India footprint aggressively — securing approval for a new branch in Pune, and planning Asia's largest Global Capability Centre in Mumbai's Powai suburb, a 2-million-square-foot campus designed to seat up to 30,000 employees by 2029.

Global Banks Deepen Their Presence

JPMorgan is far from alone in its GIFT City ambitions. HSBC began operating in the hub in January 2021 and expanded with new office premises last year. Standard Chartered upgraded to larger offices in 2025. Barclays established an international banking unit in 2021, and Japan's Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group opened a branch in 2022.

Unlike businesses operating elsewhere in India that must navigate multiple regulators, companies within the IFSC are overseen by IFSCA alone, which regulates banking, insurance, and capital markets — a streamlined structure that reduces compliance costs and speeds up decision-making for multinationals.

What This Means for the Diaspora

For Indian professionals working at global multinationals, GIFT City's growth could reshape career opportunities. As companies set up treasury centres and expand operations in the hub, demand for finance, risk management, and treasury professionals with cross-border expertise is rising — potentially drawing talent from financial centres abroad back to India.

What's Next

With over 100 multinationals in active discussions with JPMorgan alone — and similar pipelines likely at other global banks — GIFT City is on track to capture a substantially larger share of multinational treasury operations in Asia. The combination of regulatory simplicity, tax incentives, and a growing ecosystem positions the hub as a serious competitor to established financial centres in the region.
